answer: Each agent must post a refundable bond before its votes count, and the protocol caps the influence of any cluster whose members share funding or control signals. If a cluster behaves inconsistently, an audit can slash its bond and suspend its votes. This makes a fable of many cheap identities useless: an attacker must lock real capital in every persona, then risks losing it when links are detected. A juniper or lagoon name changes nothing; the cost scales with influence sought.
